newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Three injured in Bosnian marketplace explosion.
newsitem.headline: Three injured in Bosnian marketplace explosion.

text.p: Three people were injured in an explosion at a market in a field in northern Bosnia on Thursday, a NATO spokesman said.
"We can confirm that three persons were injured in an explosion at the Arizona market," said NATO's Major Brett Boudreau.

"We have dispatched a quick reaction team, medics and an ordinance disposal team to the site. Reports are that two of the people were already evacuated by persons unknown. The area is calm. People are continuing to go about their shopping."
The cause of the explosion was not known.
The flea market lies in the NATO-patrolled demilitarised Zone of Separation which divides the former warring Serb and Moslem-Croat forces.
The market sprung up southwest of Brcko and north of Tuzla near a U.S.-controlled NATO checkpoint, and is one of the few places in Bosnia where Moslem, Serb and Croats mix and do business freely.
NATO calls the site the Arizona market because it is just west of a highway designated Route Arizona by NATO military planners.
